name: Brown Trout
title: Brown Trout — The Ghost of the High Altitudes | Divine Fly Fishing
description: Discover the Brown Trout in Bhutan. Learn about its introduction in the 1930s, its adaptation to the Himalayas, and why it's a prized technical catch.
paragraphs: Introduced to the pristine waters of Bhutan in the 1930s, the Brown Trout (Salmo trutta) has since naturalized and thrives in the cold, high-altitude rivers of central and western Bhutan.

Found in the fast-flowing glacier-fed streams of the Paro, Haa, and Bumthang valleys, these wily fish offer a technical challenge for any angler. They are also known to inhabit high-altitude lakes, growing to impressive sizes in the serene Dagala Thousand Lakes region.
usps: Perfectly adapted to the ice-cold, oxygen-rich waters of the high Himalayas.
Renowned for their selective feeding and wily nature in clear waters.
Thriving in high-altitude lakes located at 4,000 meters above sea level.

name: Snow Trout
title: Snow Trout — The Native Majesty of the Himalayas | Divine Fly Fishing
description: Discover the Snow Trout in Bhutan. Learn about its evolutionary adaptation to torrential mountain streams and its importance in Himalayan biodiversity.
paragraphs: The Snow Trout (Schizothorax) is a native Himalayan species that has adapted perfectly to the torrential, ice-cold mountain streams of Bhutan.

Unlike its namesake, it is a member of the carp family with evolutionary adaptations for high-altitude white water. Found in the northern and central regions, it is a cornerstone of the Kingdom's indigenous aquatic biodiversity and a fascinating catch for seasoned anglers.
usps: Specialized for feeding in the turbulent, fast-flowing glacial rivers of the North.
An indigenous species that reflects the evolutionary history of the Himalayas.
Often released in sacred white-water rivers during rituals of merit.

name: Golden Mahseer
title: Golden Mahseer — The King of Himalayan Rivers | Divine Fly Fishing
description: Discover the Golden Mahseer in Bhutan. Learn about its sacred status, pristine habitats, and why it's the ultimate prize for catch-and-release fly fishing.
paragraphs: The Golden Mahseer (Tor putitora) is a primarily river-going fish that thrives in the subtropical glacier-fed waters of Bhutan. It is also known as the “Tiger of the Himalayan Rivers.”

Found in the major river systems of the Southern foothills, the Mahseer is a symbol of power and tenacity. Our curated trips focus on strictly enforced catch-and-release protocols to preserve this endangered ghost of the river.
usps: Navigating fierce currents and waterfalls during the spring spawning runs.
Prized by the international angling community as one of the top game fish.
Held in high spiritual regard as a protector of Bhutan's pristine waters.
